[LSIG.3.6] Under `realtime`, `gap hold` advances the integral between pump
cycles using the monotonic clock's sample at query time ([LTIM.2.8.2]). The re-evaluation is driven by
giving the rule a time-dependent condition, a positive pattern's `within` window
([LTIM.2.7.1]) or a `where` that reads a clock ([LTIM.2.4.1]), which head-inserts the
internal `$ClockTick` re-driver ([LFST.6.2]). A `then … within` window reads no
clock and drives none; `$ClockTick` is
engine-internal and not an author construct. The compiler warns
`DS_VALIDATE_SERIES_GAP_HOLD_NO_CLOCK` when a `gap hold` integral under
`realtime` has no such tick-driving window. `gap zero` and `gap skip` advance
only on assertion and need no clock.
